The proposed graph is not the maximizer, so the final answer is not correct.

**Why the construction fails.** The proposed graph is two cliques sharing one vertex, and it does satisfy both conditions. But its Nash-Williams partition has p = k+2 parts, and the partition bound only needs e(P) ≤ k(p−1) − 1 = k(k+1) − 1. The construction uses e(P) = (k+1)(k+2)/2, which is well below that bound when k ≥ 3.

**Room for more edges.** The k+1 singleton vertices of the small clique could each be joined to more vertices of the big clique. The number of singleton-to-big-clique edges t is limited only by C(k+1, 2) + t ≤ k(k+1) − 1, so t can go up to about (k²+k)/2 − 1. The proposed graph uses just k+1 of these. Adding such edges keeps the graph (k+1)-edge-connected and keeps τ < k, and it strictly increases the spectral radius, because adding an edge to a connected graph increases the spectral radius.

So the proposed graph is not extremal, and its edge count C(n−k−1, 2) + C(k+2, 2) cannot be the answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
